playbook:
My playbook for "Win As Much As You Can":

- When the opening talk phase comes, I broadcast [pledge: y]. If the others pledge Y, matching that pledge locks in the best joint outcome: everyone +1 per round, which compounds hugely on the x3, x5 and x10 rounds. This worked perfectly — three strangers all pledged Y and honored it all game, and I finished +25.

- When a pick is put to me and I have pledged Y and others are honoring Y, I pick [pick: y] every round — including the high-multiplier rounds. All-Y on a x10 round is +10 to everyone; that is far too valuable to risk for a one-shot defection of +30 (solo X) that only pays if nobody else defects and burns the trust built over nine rounds.

- I do not defect early to "test" the others. Early solo X pays only +3 while destroying the cooperative equilibrium that is worth far more across the multiplier rounds. The first ten rounds of clean all-Y were worth more than any early grab.

- I do not defect at the x3 or x5 rounds either. Defecting solo on a x5 round would gain +15, but if even one other player defects with me we each get -5, and the x10 round's cooperation collapses. The guaranteed +5 from all-Y beats that gamble — this held up through both multiplier rounds in play.

- If everyone ends up stuck on X (everyone -1 per round), I use the next talk phase to push a reset: broadcast [pledge: y] and actually play Y. Unilateral Y while others play X costs me only -1 (same as all-X) and signals the way back to all-Y.

- No defections after the second-to-last talk phase at all. Play straight Y through the final high-multiplier round. In the last round I picked Y with a tie at the top and it was correct: the marginal gain from defecting is smaller than the risk of dropping from +10 to -30 if anyone else defects too.

- A four-way tie counts as a good result, not a failure. The game's payoff structure makes all-Y the dominant joint strategy; my job is to win or tie by being the most reliable cooperator, never the first defector, and never a defector before a multiplier round. If the table ever wavers (a pledge of x, a missed Y), I re-evaluate — but as long as all three others keep pledging and playing Y, I stay the course without exception.

- Keep my talk-phase messages confident and public: reaffirming Y at every talk phase reinforced the cooperation and cost nothing. Do this at all four talk phases, not just the first.

- Watch for a lone X in any round's history. A single defection by another player is the first sign the equilibrium is breaking; if one appears, I reassess before the next multiplier round rather than assuming it was noise. In this episode there were none, so the watch never triggered — but I keep it.

WIN AS MUCH AS YOU CAN -- you, Ash, Beck and Coda; 10 rounds.
Each round every player simultaneously picks X or Y. Payoffs depend on how many picked X:
  1 X: the X gets +3, each Y gets -1
  2 X: each X +2, each Y -2
  3 X: each X +1, the Y gets -3
  4 X: everyone -1        0 X: everyone +1
Rounds 5, 8 and 10 score x3, x5 and x10.
Before rounds 1, 5, 8 and 10 there is a talk phase: each player broadcasts one pledge -- [pledge: x], [pledge: y] or [pledge: none]. A pledge is a statement of what you will pick until the next talk phase.
Highest total after 10 rounds wins. The referee validates the tokens and pays the table above.

Your broadcast. Reply with [pledge: x], [pledge: y] or [pledge: none].

Reply with the bracketed token only. One short line of reasoning before it is fine.
